Yesterday, $BTC saw another $300M in ETF outflows.

quote.text:
$BTC and $ETH are on a massive ETF outflow streak.

BTC has seen -$2B in outflows in the past 7 trading days alone.

ETH has also lost about -$1B the past 2 weeks.

Big outflows at local highs/lows can be a sign of absorption or a local reversal area but only if you actually see price stall.

As long as price keeps bleeding as the outflows keep going that just means the selling is adding onto the downside momentum.

When price stalls and outflows keep going, that's when you should be watching closely.

tweets.text:
You can be right about direction and still get liquidated before the move happens

That's the problem “Futures without liquidation” is trying to solve

So, let's talk about how it works:

CASE STUDY

Let's say you open a BTC long because you are expecting a pump

> Traditional futures: Price drops, liquidates you, and finally goes up without you

> Futures without liquidation: Price drops, your position loses value, but the drop doesn't force a liquidation

When you open a trade, you choose an expiry date. You can close earlier or let it settle at expiry.

That means:

If BTC recovers while the contract is still open, your position can recover value too
But, if your contract expires on Friday, a recovery on Saturday is too late.

HOW IT WORKS

The product uses options underneath to give exposure similar to futures

That's why it has an expiry date and no margin liquidation level

You are paying for that exposure over a specific period of time

Staying longer means opening a new contract and paying for more time

COSTS

Costs include:

> 0.01% of position value when opening and closing
> The spread
> Funding to expiration (shown before entry)

So 0.01% isn't the total cost of the trade.

MY OPINION

I think this could be useful for the traders who have conviction about a move, but expect a lot of volatility along the way

You can still lose money, no liquidation doesn't mean no losses

A man always needs a plan

That said, it's an interesting tool. I will keep exploring it and sharing my experience.

Would you use it for your trades?

https://clickoptions.ai/?ref=9wtjCyU

Not buying any major quantities of Bitcoin until/if we reach the $66,700 price level.

quote.text:
There is absolutely no demand for Bitcoin between roughly $73,500 and $66,700.

$73,500 happens to be the 200-day moving average, which is the good news. As long as we stay above that level, BTC should be fine. But losing it could drag the price down another 9.5%.

What am I doing? I’m already long Bitcoin and have limit orders set to keep buying all the way down toward (potentially) $60,800. I’ll be a buyer on any further correction.

I strongly believe 2027-2029 will be fantastic for the asset class. My goal is to build a macro long position ahead of a strong push over the next year and a half.
